stories.headline: Bengaluru screenings of Pakistani drama Dar-e-Nijaat cancelled after online backlash
stories.dek: Separately, the All Indian Cine Workers Association has asked the Prime Minister to block Netflix's Pakistani series Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo in India.
stories.summary: Organisers called off two Bengaluru screenings of the Pakistani drama Dar-e-Nijaat, planned for November 28 and December 5, after social media objections. AICWA has written to PM Narendra Modi seeking a ban on Fawad Khan's Netflix series, which he called a 'win for Pakistan'.
body: Organisers cancelled two private screenings of the Pakistani television drama Dar-e-Nijaat in Bengaluru, planned for November 28 and December 5, after objections on social media and an inquiry by city police, according to The News Minute, NDTV and PTI.

The first event, by The Bloom Society Sisters' Club, was to be held at Sheeshkebab restaurant in Frazer Town on November 28. Billed as the "First Ever Screening in Bangalore", it was to show episodes 34 and 35, followed by a Persian and Arabic dinner. The News Minute reported tickets at Rs 1,999 per person. A restaurant representative said the event would not go ahead but gave no detailed reason.
The second, by The Star Club, was set for December 5 at a private theatre. Promotional material reportedly listed Pakistani outfits as the dress code.

Bengaluru Police Commissioner R Hitendra said police had taken note of the plans. "As of now, something is being organised. We are getting in touch with the organisers to know more details about it. If anything needs to be done on the ground, it will be done," he said, as quoted by NDTV.

The December 5 host, who did not wish to be named, told PTI the event was meant for family and close friends. She said police had not contacted her and that she cancelled after seeing the online discussion. NDTV quoted the host as saying: "Since this has become an issue, we have decided to cancel the screening." There has been no official police statement announcing action against either event, The News Minute reported.

Separately, the All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on November 24, seeking a ban on Netflix's first Pakistani original, Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo. The letter, signed by president Suresh Shyamlal Gupta, was also marked to Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and Netflix India. It cited the ministry's advisory of May 8, 2025 asking OTT platforms to stop streaming Pakistan-origin content, and called for a permanent law with the severest penalties.

The Federation of Western India Cine Employees, which describes itself as an umbrella body of 32 associations, said it would also write to the Prime Minister. Its president, B N Tiwari, told PTI that if the show is released in India, "we will ensure that the shoot of all the Netflix projects comes to a halt here".

At the trailer launch in Karachi on Tuesday, Fawad Khan said: "It's a win for Pakistan, and I'm very glad and honoured to be a part of it." Co-star Hania Aamir called the series "a stepping stone for us".

Hindustan Times reported that as of November 25 the series could be viewed on Netflix India's website but did not appear on the app. Netflix has not said whether it will be available to Indian subscribers. The first part premieres on December 4.

It is Netflix's first Pakistani original. AICWA's letter also referred to restrictions on Pakistani artists after the Pulwama and Pahalgam attacks.

stories.headline: Gordon Ramsay to lead revived Top Gear, due on screens in 2028
stories.dek: The BBC show has been off air since Andrew Flintoff's 2022 crash; Ramsay's co-presenters have not yet been named.
stories.summary: The BBC said on Wednesday that chef Gordon Ramsay will lead a revived Top Gear, with filming next year and broadcast in 2028. The show has been off air since Andrew Flintoff's crash in December 2022.
body: The BBC announced on Wednesday that the chef Gordon Ramsay will lead a revived Top Gear, with filming due to start next year and the series set to reach screens in 2028.
Ramsay, 60, will be joined by co-presenters who have not yet been named. The BBC said they will be announced in due course.

The motoring show has been off air since December 2022, when Andrew Flintoff suffered serious facial and rib injuries after the open-topped Morgan Super 3 he was driving overturned at the Dunsfold Aerodrome test track. The BBC apologised and paid compensation to Flintoff, according to the BBC's own report. The Guardian said it is understood he received compensation.

In a statement, Ramsay said he grew up near the Silverstone circuit in Northamptonshire. "I would climb over the fences and sneak in for a glimpse of the racing," he said. He said he wants to bring "a fresh energy and ambition" to the show.
Ramsay owns cars including several Aston Martins and Ferraris, a Porsche, a Land Rover and a McLaren Senna. He has appeared on Top Gear as a guest three times, in 2002, 2006 and 2017.

Ed Havard, the BBC's director of entertainment, said: "Gordon's fierce and fearless approach makes him a natural fit." Suzy Lamb, managing director of BBC Studios Entertainment, said the series "won't be a nostalgic reboot".

The BBC said the new series will include "epic adventures, daring tests and spectacular stunts". It confirmed that familiar features such as the Stig will return. The Guardian reported that a health and safety review followed Flintoff's accident.

Former host Richard Hammond told BBC Radio 4's PM programme that the BBC approached him about leading the new show. "I don't want to drag it back to what it was," he said, explaining why he declined. He also said Top Gear "doesn't have to be" a dangerous programme.

Comedian Jimmy Carr had been rumoured to be in talks to join the line-up but was reported on Tuesday to have "pulled out", according to the BBC. The Guardian said the former England rugby player Joe Marler had also been mooted.
Separately, Ramsay has been confirmed for an ITV revival of Hell's Kitchen, hosted by Claudia Winkleman.

stories.headline: Tamil song 'Varuvaaiy' gets Grammy nomination; original composer's credit questioned
stories.dek: After the composer's son said his father was not credited, the producer and singer have named L. Krishnan in Instagram notes.
stories.summary: 'Varuvaaiy' is the first Tamil song nominated for a Grammy, in the Best Global Music Performance category. After questions over the omission of original composer L. Krishnan, producer Devan Ekambaram and singer Susha acknowledged him on Instagram.
body: 'Varuvaaiy', a rendition of a song based on Subramania Bharati's verse, has become the first Tamil song nominated for a Grammy, and its producer and singer have now credited the original composer, L. Krishnan, after his son raised the omission.

The track is the only Indian entry at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards. It is among the final five nominees in the Best Global Music Performance category, alongside entries by Angélique Kidjo, Pharrell Williams, Shakira and Burna Boy. The awards will be held on February 7, 2027.

Devan Ekambaram is the arranger and producer, and Susha (Subiksha Rangarajan) sings. The contemporary orchestration features Anil Srinivasan on piano, Prakash Sontakke on slide guitar, Joseph John on bass and Sarvajit Krishna Mohan on tabla.

After the nominations were announced, Krishnan's son, K. Arun Prakash, said in an Instagram video that the tune was his father's. He said Krishnan composed it in Raag Desh for Carnatic vocalist Nithyasree Mahadevan around 1989 or 1990, for her album of Bharatiyar songs.
“It is hurtful that my father was not given due credit,” he said. “I understand that his name has now been included, but this should have been done when the decision to use the song was made.”

Susha said in an Instagram post that she learnt the song as a girl from her mother, the musician Lakshmi Rangarajan, who had learnt it from an audio tape of Nithyasree. “It was set to tune by Krishnan mama, who is a very loved tunesmith,” she said.
The Hindu reported on November 25 that Ekambaram and Susha had since acknowledged Krishnan in notes on their Instagram handles.

The Recording Academy requires entries in the category to be new recordings, released within the eligibility period and recorded no more than five years before release. The song itself need not be new, and covers, folk and traditional pieces and reinterpretations can qualify, according to The Hindu.

The Grammy Awards will be held on February 7, 2027.
stories.background: The category was formerly called Best World Music Performance. The Recording Academy changed the name, saying 'world music' carried colonial connotations. Ekambaram became a voting member of the Recording Academy in July this year, The Hindu reported.
stories.whyItMatters: The nomination brings a Tamil song into international music discussions, and the credit question touches on how original composers of older works are acknowledged when their tunes are reused.

stories.headline: Netflix releases trailer for Imtiaz Ali's 'O Saathi Re', out on December 4
stories.dek: The six-part series stars Aditi Rao Hydari and Avinash Tiwary as a couple heading for divorce, with Arjun Rampal playing a man who enters Roshni's life.
stories.summary: Netflix has released the trailer for O Saathi Re, a six-part series created by Imtiaz Ali and directed by Arif Ali. It stars Aditi Rao Hydari, Avinash Tiwary and Arjun Rampal and premieres on December 4.
body: Netflix released the trailer on Wednesday for O Saathi Re, a six-part series created and showrun by Imtiaz Ali, starring Aditi Rao Hydari, Avinash Tiwary and Arjun Rampal, which premieres on the streaming service on December 4.
Arif Ali has directed the series. Imtiaz Ali co-wrote it with Amogh Kanaskar and Nidhi Sethia, according to Hindustan Times.

The trailer introduces Roshni, played by Hydari, and Karan Naagar, played by Tiwary. NDTV reported that it opens and closes with the two sitting in a family court, seeking a divorce. Flashbacks set in a hill town show their early romance and marriage.

Rampal plays Pradyuman. As Roshni moves into a more affluent social world, she meets a man who is drawn to her, NDTV said. In the trailer she says she had always tried to be the "good girl", and that this began to suffocate her.

The trailer also shows Karan struggling with feelings of inadequacy. NDTV said he describes Roshni as thriving in a "high-class world" while he remains outside it. It ends with a judge asking whether both consent to the divorce.

Imtiaz Ali has called the show "a modern romantic show with a vintage heart". The title comes from Kishore Kumar's song in Muqaddar Ka Sikandar, which also helped inspire the series, Hindustan Times reported.
Of the emotions behind the story, Ali said in an interview: "When a relationship breaks, there is mourning. Mourning is due to love. There is a feeling of incompleteness."

Tiwary said Karan's love is absolute and that Roshni is his world. Hydari described Roshni as "a woman trying to understand herself beyond the roles she has always played in other people's lives". Rampal said Pradyuman is "confident, self-assured" and that there is more to him than meets the eye.

The series is produced by Window Seat Films. Imtiaz Ali, Mohit Choudhary and Shibasish Sarkar back it, with Vishal Bajaj and Pratik Nandkumar More as executive producers and Sethia as creative producer.

stories.headline: Nigerian actor Pete Edochie dies at 79 after prostate cancer battle
stories.dek: The Nollywood star, best known for playing Okonkwo in the 1987 television adaptation of Things Fall Apart, died in Enugu, his family said.
stories.summary: Pete Edochie, one of Nollywood's best-known actors, died in Enugu on Wednesday aged 79 after a long battle with prostate cancer, his family said. Tributes have come from fans, fellow actors and Enugu State's governor.
body: Pete Edochie, the Nigerian actor who became one of the best-known faces of Nollywood, died aged 79 in the south-eastern city of Enugu on Wednesday, his family said.

In a statement posted on Instagram by his son Leo, the family said he died at 12.30am on November 25 after a protracted battle with prostate cancer. The statement was titled "An Iroko Has Fallen". It said funeral arrangements would be announced in due course.

Edochie began his career as a broadcaster in 1967 before moving into acting. He rose to prominence in 1987 as Okonkwo, the Igbo warrior in a television adaptation of Chinua Achebe's novel Things Fall Apart, which won him recognition beyond Nigeria.

He was known for playing traditional rulers, wealthy businessmen and family patriarchs, and for his deep voice and use of African proverbs. His films included Igodo, Rituals, Billionaire's Club and the 2018 romantic comedy Lionheart. In 2003 he received the national honour Member of the Order of the Niger. He also won the Industry Merit Award at the Africa Magic Viewers' Choice Awards.
In recent years, his expressions and lines from his films reached a younger audience through social media memes, BBC News reported.

Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah called his death a huge loss to Nigeria. He praised Edochie for introducing international audiences to Igbo traditions and inspiring younger performers. "Pete Edochie was more than an accomplished actor, he was an institution," Mbah said.
Abubakar Yakubu, president of the Actors Guild of Nigeria, described Edochie as a "father figure" in the industry and said his influence would be felt for generations.
Edochie had spoken publicly in October, during a visit to Ghana, about his declining health, saying he was struggling to walk and had swelling in parts of his body.
He is survived by his wife, Josephine, and their six children, including the actors Yul and Linc Edochie.
keyFacts: Pete Edochie died aged 79 at 12.30am on Wednesday, November 25, in Enugu.
His family said the cause was a protracted battle with prostate cancer.
He rose to fame in 1987 playing Okonkwo in Things Fall Apart.
He received the Member of the Order of the Niger in 2003.
Funeral arrangements are yet to be announced.

stories.headline: Bengaluru tunnel road to skip Lalbagh as two alternative routes are surveyed
stories.dek: Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said the realignment may raise costs, while the state's contribution stays fixed at ₹7,000 crore and talks with the contractor continue.
stories.summary: Karnataka Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said on Wednesday the Hebbal-Silk Board tunnel road will be moved out of Lalbagh, with two alternative alignments being surveyed. The government is also negotiating with the contractor to reduce the project cost.
body: Karnataka's Bengaluru development minister, Krishna Byre Gowda, said on Wednesday that the proposed Hebbal-Silk Board tunnel road will not use Lalbagh land, and that the government is surveying two alternative alignments.

"The alignment will definitely be changed, so there is no need for any confusion about that," Gowda told reporters. "We have given the people a promise through the Hon'ble Chief Minister that we will move it outside Lalbagh." The Hindustan Times reported that areas around Siddapura and Wilson Garden are among those being considered. The exact locations and the final route have not been announced.

The original plan for the 16.75-km road involved entry and exit ramps at Lalbagh, which would have required garden land. Environmentalists, walkers and citizens' groups protested. In August 2026, thousands formed a human chain around Lalbagh Rock. The Cabinet earlier this month resolved to exclude Lalbagh and withdrew the Karnataka Parks Conservation Amendment Bill, which would have allowed park land to be used for infrastructure.

Gowda said the government would consult stakeholders and finalise one of the two options as soon as possible. The revised alignment must go to the Cabinet for approval before a work order is issued. He said the contractor would then need considerable time to mobilise resources before construction begins.

The alternative route is likely to be longer, Gowda said, and so cost more. "The change in alignment may increase the project cost, but toll charges will not be increased," he said, according to the Hindustan Times. The News Minute reported he said the toll would remain as fixed by the National Highways authorities, though the collection period could vary slightly.

A Cabinet-constituted committee headed by the Chief Secretary, with Finance and Public Works Department officials, is negotiating rates with the contractor. It has held one or two rounds of talks. Adani Enterprises is the lowest bidder for two packages, at ₹22,000 crore, South First reported. Gowda said the state will contribute only ₹7,000 crore regardless of the quote, though how any extra cost from the new route is shared remains to be decided.

Bengaluru South MP Tejasvi Surya of the BJP welcomed the move as "an initial victory for the citizens' movement". He said opposition to the project itself would continue, citing warnings from IISc and other experts that it will worsen congestion, and challenged Gowda to a public debate.

Activist AN Yellappa Reddy, who led the protests, asked what the basis was for persisting with the project and called for public consultation and independent technical scrutiny, including on the impact on groundwater systems.

stories.background: The tunnel road was initiated by Chief Minister DK Shivakumar after the Congress returned to power in 2023, according to South First. The original alignment passed beneath Lalbagh, with a cut-and-cover section on the entry ramp and another on the exit ramp, according to the Detailed Project Report cited by South First.
stories.whyItMatters: The choice of route will decide the project's cost and how any increase is shared, and it determines whether Lalbagh is affected. Final approval and the work order depend on the Cabinet.

stories.headline: ASHA workers' Bengaluru protest enters ninth day after government appeal fails
stories.dek: Protesters at Freedom Park say they will stay until the government gives a written assurance on a ₹15,000 monthly honorarium, even as dozens fall ill.
stories.summary: ASHA workers protesting at Bengaluru's Freedom Park for a ₹15,000 monthly honorarium rejected Chief Minister DK Shivakumar's video-call appeal to withdraw. At least 200 have sought medical help after days in the cold and rain.
body: ASHA workers protesting at Freedom Park in Bengaluru entered a ninth day on Wednesday, refusing to end their agitation for a ₹15,000 monthly honorarium after Chief Minister DK Shivakumar appealed to them to withdraw it.

The workers began the protest on November 17. They are demanding a pay revision and a written assurance from the government, according to South First. Press Trust of India reported that the government's appeals to end the protest had failed.

Shivakumar, who is in Japan, spoke to the protesters by video call on Tuesday. "I have special concern for ASHA workers. We will certainly find a solution to your problems. Have faith in me and withdraw the protest," he said. He added that he would discuss their demands with the Finance Department during the Assembly session. The workers stayed firm on their demand for a written assurance.

Hundreds of workers have spent their nights at the site, many sleeping under blue tarpaulins. Rain began at 3 pm on Tuesday, and the workers first used the tarpaulins for cover. As it grew heavier in the evening, police helped them move to a parking lot.

Volunteers running a medical camp at the site said at least 200 workers have sought treatment for fever, cough, chills and runny nose. Dr Sujith Kumar, a volunteer doctor, said workers have also reported urinary tract infections, blood pressure fluctuations and back pain. "We are sending people who have fallen seriously ill to the KC General Hospital," he told South First.
Five workers have been taken to KC General Hospital in the past two days. Two had fainted, two had fever, and one complained of shortness of breath and chest pain.
Shobha, an ASHA worker from Mandya district who has spent six days at the park, said she had a headache, runny nose and fever. "I will not go home until the government accepts our demands," she said.
A worker from Kalaburagi said the government had been willing to pay ₹10,000 last year but had given no concrete assurance on an increase.

Agriculture Minister PM Narendraswamy said on Tuesday that the government could not give ASHA workers a "gold necklace every time they made a demand", South First reported. Actor and former Congress MP Divya Spandana criticised the remark as insensitive when she visited the site. She said the government must honour its commitment to pay ₹10,000 a month.
The Assembly session, during which Shivakumar has said he will raise the demands with the Finance Department, is the next point at which the issue is expected to be taken up.

stories.headline: Kawasaki to invest up to ₹800 crore in Harohalli unit; Sumitomo eyes park
stories.dek: Karnataka's Chief Minister, on a Japan visit, also met JFE Engineering and Panasonic Automotive, and the state invited all three to Invest Karnataka 2027.
stories.summary: Kawasaki Heavy Industries will invest up to ₹800 crore over 10 years to expand Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery at Harohalli, adding about 600 jobs. PTI reported that Sumitomo is keen on a 100-acre industrial park near Bengaluru.
body: Kawasaki Heavy Industries will invest up to ₹800 crore over 10 years to expand Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery Pvt. Ltd. at Harohalli Industrial Area near Bengaluru, a memorandum of understanding signed in Tokyo on Wednesday showed.
The expansion is expected to create about 600 manufacturing jobs. It will add capacity for hydraulic pumps, swing motors and related components used in construction equipment.

The agreement was exchanged by S Selvakumar, Principal Secretary, Commerce and Industries Department, Kenji Matsushita of Kawasaki Heavy Industries and Minoru Hatsuda, CEO of Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery. Chief Minister D K Shivakumar and Large and Medium Industries Minister M B Patil were present.

The investment will come in two phases. South First reported that the first phase will be ₹200 crore to ₹400 crore and the second ₹400 crore to ₹800 crore. The state government will help with land allotment, approvals, clearances and applicable incentives.
Press Trust of India reported, in a headline, that Sumitomo is keen to set up a 100-acre industrial park near Bengaluru, citing a Karnataka minister. The full text of that report was not available.

Shivakumar and Patil are in Japan on an investment outreach. The Chief Minister's office said in releases on Wednesday that the delegation met JFE Engineering Corporation Managing Director Keiichi Nagaya to discuss waste-to-energy and municipal solid waste management.

JFE shared details of technology that it said can generate about 15 MW of power while reducing the waste sent to landfills. The Karnataka side expressed interest in extending such projects beyond Bengaluru to other major cities, and both sides discussed finding local partners.

The delegation also met Panasonic Automotive's President and CEO Mike Nagayasu, presenting Karnataka as a base for advanced manufacturing and Global Capability Centres. The Hindu reported that Shivakumar also met Japan's Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Yasutaka Nakasone, and invited a high-level Japanese delegation with a dedicated country pavilion.
Kawasaki and Panasonic Automotive were invited to Invest Karnataka 2027, which will be held in Bengaluru from April 20 to 22.

Karnataka has received 101 Japanese greenfield projects since 2016 and has more than 525 Japanese establishments, according to an official release. Harohalli lies in Shivakumar's Kanakapura constituency.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu signs 78 MoUs worth ₹58,214 crore at second VETTRI investors' conclave
stories.dek: The state government says the agreements, signed in the presence of Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay, will create 65,786 jobs across 25 districts.
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu signed 78 MoUs with companies pledging ₹58,214 crore on Wednesday at the second VETTRI conclave. The state says the projects will create 65,786 jobs, taking commitments since May to about ₹1.73 trillion.
body: The Tamil Nadu government signed 78 memoranda of understanding with companies on Wednesday, with proposed investments of ₹58,214 crore and 65,786 projected jobs, at the second VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investment and Conversion Conclave.
Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay oversaw the signings. Hindustan Times reported the venue as a hotel in Mahabalipuram, about 60 km from Chennai; Deccan Herald datelined its report from Chennai.

Of the 78 MoUs, 58 are for new ventures and account for 64 per cent of the investment value, Deccan Herald reported. Eighteen are for expansion of existing facilities and two combine fresh investment with expansion. The projects will be spread over 25 districts, including Dharmapuri, Virudhunagar, Cuddalore and Theni.
Fourteen companies headquartered in Brazil, Finland, Germany, Singapore, South Korea, Sweden and the United States committed foreign direct investment totalling ₹14,798 crore.

Hosur and Krishnagiri district secured about 13 projects worth ₹12,643 crore and 14,600 jobs. Titan Company pledged ₹1,500 crore for precision components for the aerospace, semiconductor and defence sectors. TVS Motor Company pledged ₹2,000 crore to expand its Hosur two-wheeler unit. POSCO is to invest ₹250 crore in a steel processing project.

Royal Enfield will set up an electric motorcycle manufacturing project with ₹1,000 crore and 500 jobs. Brazil's WEG Industries chose Dharmapuri for a proposed ₹2,000 crore facility for electric vehicle motors and industrial drives, which could create around 3,000 jobs, according to Industries Minister S Keerthana.

Keerthana said the government is focused on turning MoUs into operating projects. Of 112 MoUs signed before Wednesday, 83 had reached land allotment or beyond, a conversion rate of 74.1 per cent. She acknowledged that 25.9 per cent had not reached that stage.
“Our real competition is not another state, but the world's leading manufacturing economies,” she said. The government presented the chief minister a project-wise status report to track bottlenecks.

The event followed a claim by the opposition Bharatiya Janata Party that investments meant for Tamil Nadu are going to Andhra Pradesh. Former state BJP president Tamilisai Soundararajan said on November 22 that the government should say how many earlier MoUs had become working factories. Deccan Herald also noted reports that staff at Guidance, the state's investment promotion arm, were asked to resign over alleged leaks to Andhra Pradesh; the sources did not carry a government response to that.
Vijay also laid foundation stones for projects, including an Ultraviolette electric scooter unit in Krishnagiri district. Deccan Herald put the day's total industrial outlay at over ₹67,000 crore.

stories.headline: FIR filed against TVK MLA over alleged messages to woman IAS officer
stories.dek: The Madras High Court named an IPS officer to investigate Kallakurichi MLA C Arul Vignesh, while the government formed a complaints committee and Udhayanidhi Stalin sought his arrest.
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu police told the Madras High Court on Tuesday that an FIR was registered against Kallakurichi MLA C Arul Vignesh over a woman IAS officer's complaint. The state has formed a four-member committee, and Udhayanidhi Stalin has sought the MLA's arrest.
body: Tamil Nadu police told the Madras High Court on Tuesday that they had registered a First Information Report on Monday against Kallakurichi MLA C Arul Vignesh of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) over allegedly misbehaving with a woman IAS officer.

Justice V Lakshminarayanan recorded the submission of State Public Prosecutor R John Sathyan. He said Tiruppur Superintendent of Police Shristi Singh would investigate the case, registered at the Kallakurichi All Women Police Station. Inspector-General of Police (Administration) N Kamini will monitor the probe because the accused "holds a high position and a constitutional office", the judge said.

The Hindu reported that police sources said the case was booked under Sections 75, 78 and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. South First reported that the complaint alleges inappropriate WhatsApp messages, unwanted advances and an attempt to visit the officer's official residence at night. Arul Vignesh has denied the allegations, calling them false and politically motivated.

The court said the officer had formally complained at about 3 p.m. on Monday, after the judge asked the prosecutor on Monday how a prosecution could proceed without her complaint. The judge directed the Chief Secretary to constitute an Internal Complaints Committee under the POSH Act.

On Wednesday, South First reported, the state constituted a four-member committee headed by Additional Chief Secretary Kakarla Usha. Its other members are S Madumathi, IAS; P Sumathi, Secretary, Law Department; and Sunitha Joe. It has 60 days to complete the inquiry.

The judge also barred the media from disclosing the identity of the complainant or witnesses under Section 16 of the POSH Act and ordered the police cyber crime wing to have related social media posts removed. "The press could have shown some sensitivity in a matter like this," he said.

Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin submitted a complaint to the Director General of Police on Wednesday seeking the MLA's immediate arrest and a Central Bureau of Investigation probe. He said it took 116 days for police to register an FIR and alleged that the government led by Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay had tried to cover up the matter.

Udhayanidhi also alleged that the officer had complained in July and that Chief Secretary M Sai Kumar asked her to seek a transfer instead of acting. He sought action against the Chief Secretary. The sources did not carry a response from the government or the Chief Secretary to these claims.
The High Court will hear the case next on Friday, November 27. The National Commission for Women has asked the Director-General of Police for an action-taken report within seven days.

stories.headline: CMRL floats tenders to finish entry and exit works at Phase II elevated stations
stories.dek: The agency has also delayed first trains on part of the Yellow Line by an hour to speed up testing at seven stations.
stories.summary: Chennai Metro Rail Limited has floated tenders to complete pending architectural works, including entry and exit facilities, at newly opened Phase II elevated stations. It has also pushed back morning services on part of the Yellow Line to 7 am.
body: Chennai Metro Rail Limited (CMRL) has floated tenders to complete the balance architectural works, including entry and exit facilities, at the newly opened elevated stations under Phase II, DT Next reported.

The tendered works also cover pending repairs and infrastructure-related requirements meant to improve passenger convenience. CMRL said the remaining work would be taken up at the newly operational stations so that all passenger facilities are completed.

For some stations, entry and exit work, including escalators and lifts, is pending, according to CMRL. The agency said these would be addressed promptly. It will also conduct inspections to identify and resolve issues and demands raised by commuters.

Passenger services began in October on the Yellow Line between Poonamallee Bypass and Porur Junction. Train operations have started on the stretch, but some architectural and associated works at the stations remain incomplete.
Separately, CMRL has temporarily revised morning timings on the Yellow Line from Tuesday. Services between Poonamallee Bypass and Porur Junction now start at 7 am instead of 6 am.

The revised schedule is meant to allow construction and testing at the remaining seven stations in the Porur Junction–Vadapalani section. The longer block hours will let CMRL speed up essential testing, including of the Automatic Signalling System needed for Unattended Train Operations (UTO).
CMRL said the changes were necessary to speed up commissioning and improve connectivity along the stretch. It acknowledged the inconvenience to passengers.

stories.headline: Supreme Court gives Centre, Delhi government 10 days to answer pleas on protest detentions
stories.dek: Petitioners will have a week after that to file rejoinders, the bench said, after the government's counsel told the court affidavits had been filed in only some of the cases.
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday directed the Centre and the Delhi government to file a comprehensive response within 10 days to petitions over detentions during the October 10 anti-CEC protests. Delhi Police has told the court no one was arrested or detained that day.
body: The Supreme Court on Wednesday directed the Centre and the Delhi government to file a comprehensive response within 10 days to petitions alleging detentions, particularly of political leaders, during the October 10 protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in New Delhi.
A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana passed the order. It asked petitioners to file any rejoinders within a week after the government's response.
The direction followed a submission by Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati that affidavits had been filed in only some of the petitions relating to the detentions.

Delhi Police has told the court that a habeas corpus petition filed by Trinamool Congress MP and lawyer Menaka Guruswamy has become infructuous. The petition concerns the alleged removal of former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee from the protest site. Police said no one was arrested or detained during the October 10 protests.
Outlook reported that the pleas also include allegations of custodial assault. The other outlets did not mention that allegation.

The protest call was given by the CJP and some student organisations over alleged irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission. The three outlets reported that the planned mass mobilisation at Jantar Mantar on October 11 was thwarted by a security clampdown and the detention of more than 7,000 protesters. Those detained included CJP leader Abhijit Dipke, several opposition leaders and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee.
The reports do not reconcile the police statement that no one was detained on October 10 with the detention of more than 7,000 people reported for October 11.

In a special sitting on October 11, the Supreme Court had said people gathering peacefully should not be illegally detained. It also asked the Centre to ensure the Delhi Metro functioned normally and that internet services were not disrupted, subject to law-and-order conditions.

stories.headline: Nearly 9 in 10 women feel unsafe walking to Delhi metro and bus stops, survey finds
stories.dek: The Centre for Equity and Inclusion also found 88.9 per cent felt unsafe in their nearest public park after dark, and has sent recommendations to the Supreme Court.
stories.summary: A survey of 1,588 women, girls and LGBTQ+ people in Delhi by the Centre for Equity and Inclusion found 87.5 per cent feel unsafe walking to the nearest metro station or bus stop. The organisation has submitted recommendations to the Supreme Court.
body: A survey by the gender equality organisation Centre for Equity and Inclusion (CEQUIN) found that 87.5 per cent of women, girls and LGBTQ+ people surveyed in Delhi feel unsafe walking to the nearest metro station or bus stop, according to a statement from the group.

The study, based on responses from 1,588 people, also found that 88.9 per cent felt unsafe in their nearest public park after dark. More than three-fourths reported poorly lit footpaths, and 60 per cent said footpaths were broken or missing.

For nearly 80 per cent of respondents, men's behaviour, including staring, passing comments and following them, made everyday journeys unsafe. About 80.5 per cent could not identify the civic authority responsible for addressing their concerns.

The study is titled 'Everyday Journeys: Women's and Girls' Access to Footpaths and Public Parks in Delhi'. CEQUIN said it looks beyond individual crimes to how the design and upkeep of public spaces, social behaviour and gaps in institutional accountability limit women's movement.

"When over 80 per cent of respondents cannot even identify which civic authority is responsible for addressing these gaps, exclusion becomes built into the city itself," said Lora K Prabhu, CEQUIN's co-founder and managing director. She said the organisation hoped its recommendations would drive measurable, gender-responsive urban reform.

The report cites National Crime Records Bureau data showing Delhi recorded 13,396 crimes against women in 2024, the highest among India's 19 major metropolitan cities. It also notes Delhi's female Labour Force Participation Rate was 14.5 per cent in 2023-24, against 54 per cent for men. The report argues safety fears and restricted mobility affect women's access to employment, though the figures do not establish a direct causal link.

CEQUIN said the study was undertaken in response to the Supreme Court's intervention after a series of rape and sexual assault cases in Delhi-NCR. The court took suo motu cognisance on September 28 and directed authorities to identify vulnerable public spaces and strengthen safety measures.
The study was due to be released on Wednesday at CEQUIN's annual event, 'Hain Haq Hamara Hissedari', which marks the start of the '16 Days of Activism' against gender-based violence.

The Supreme Court took suo motu cognisance on September 28 and directed authorities to identify vulnerable public spaces and strengthen safety measures.
stories.whyItMatters: The findings point to infrastructure gaps such as poor lighting and broken footpaths, and to unclear civic responsibility, as factors in how women move around Delhi. CEQUIN has placed its recommendations before the Supreme Court, which is examining public space safety.

stories.dek: Four hospitals reported 913 lung cancer deaths between January 2020 and July 2026, about one every three days, according to replies to PTI Bhasha's RTI applications.
stories.summary: Three major Delhi hospitals recorded 6,581 lung cancer cases from January 2020 to mid-2026, averaging 83 a month, RTI replies show. Across four hospitals, 913 deaths were reported, equal to one every three days.
body: Three of four leading Delhi hospitals recorded 6,581 lung cancer cases between January 1, 2020, and July 31, 2026, an average of 83 a month, according to replies to Right to Information applications filed by PTI Bhasha.

The four institutions, AIIMS, RML Hospital, Safdarjung Hospital and the Delhi State Cancer Institute (DSCI), reported 913 deaths in total, or one patient every three days. Safdarjung gave only its death count, 393, and did not disclose total cases, so the case figure covers the other three.
AIIMS reported the most cases: 4,860 from January 2020 to March 2026, with 158 deaths. That is about 65 cases and two deaths a month.

The DSCI reported 1,613 cases between January 1, 2020, and July 2026, with 354 deaths, or about 20 cases and four deaths a month. It said two children were diagnosed in 2021 and that 351 women had lung cancer over the period. It gave no gender breakdown of deaths.
RML Hospital reported 108 cases, including 47 women, and eight deaths.
The applicants also asked for data on patients who had never smoked. None of the institutes provided it.

A senior DSCI doctor, speaking to PTI on condition of anonymity, said the institute treats patients from Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Bihar and Nepal as well as Delhi. The doctor said smoking or exposure to tobacco smoke is the primary cause, with genetic mutations also playing a role.

Doctors said lung cancer has also been found in women who do not smoke, and that this is suspected to be linked to genetic mutations and pollution. They said the disease is often diagnosed only at a late stage, which makes treatment very difficult.

Dr Geeta Kadayaprath of the Apollo Athenaa Women's Cancer Centre said long-term exposure to polluted air can raise the risk. She noted that the International Agency for Research on Cancer, part of the World Health Organization, classifies outdoor air pollution and its particulate matter as carcinogenic to humans. PM 2.5 particles, she said, can penetrate deep into the lungs and damage cells over time.

Dr Vikas Maurya of Fortis Hospital, Shalimar Bagh, said early stages often show no clear symptoms. Warning signs include a persistent cough, coughing up blood, shortness of breath, chest pain, voice changes, unexplained weight loss and recurring chest infections. He said a standard X-ray cannot detect the condition and a CT scan is required.
keyFacts: 6,581 lung cancer cases were recorded at AIIMS, RML and the Delhi State Cancer Institute.
Four hospitals reported 913 deaths between January 2020 and July 2026.
AIIMS recorded 4,860 cases and 158 deaths from January 2020 to March 2026.
Safdarjung Hospital reported 393 deaths but gave no case total.
No hospital supplied data on lung cancer patients who never smoked.
stories.background: November is observed as Lung Cancer Awareness Month, and Delhi is facing severe air pollution this season. Health experts say long-term exposure to polluted air raises lung cancer risk but is not the sole cause; smoking and genetic mutations are others.
stories.whyItMatters: Doctors say lung cancer is often found only in late stages and has no clear early symptoms, which makes diagnosis by CT scan important for those with warning signs.

stories.headline: Women's commission asks Telangana Governor to recommend special probe into egg racket
stories.dek: The panel also wants a high-level committee and changes to the Assisted Reproductive Technology Act, citing gaps in how the law is implemented.
stories.summary: The Telangana State Women's Commission met Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla on Wednesday and asked him to recommend a special investigation into the alleged illegal egg retrieval racket in Hyderabad. The Governor sought details and said he would consult the state government.
body: The Telangana State Women's Commission on Wednesday asked Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla to recommend a special investigation into the alleged illegal oocyte (egg) retrieval racket in Hyderabad, citing its interstate reach.

Commission chairperson Nerella Sharada and member Uzma Shakeer met the Governor at Lok Bhavan and briefed him on the commission's inquiry, information from officials, the police investigation and court developments, according to a commission release.

The commission asked for a high-level committee to ensure what the release called a comprehensive and impartial investigation. It also said the Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) Act has loopholes and shortcomings in its implementation, and urged the Governor to recommend amendments to better protect women's rights, health and safety.

Sharada said women from different states were allegedly brought to Hyderabad with promises of jobs, including event work, and then persuaded to undergo illegal egg retrieval by exploiting their financial vulnerability. The commission said poor and middle-class women were particularly targeted and that a significant number of women across the country had been affected.

Sharada also told the Governor that the High Court had denied anticipatory bail to the accused. The Times of India reported that the petitions were filed by three doctors who run fertility centres in Hyderabad.

The Governor responded positively and sought detailed information, the commission said. He assured the delegation that he would discuss the issue with officials of the departments concerned and consult the state government so that appropriate action is initiated.

Malkajgiri police said on October 31 that they had busted the racket and arrested eight people. The accused allegedly recruited women from West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh and other states and housed them for egg donation procedures at IVF and fertility centres.

The number of women rescued is reported differently. PTI and The Hindu put it at 43; The Times of India reported 48. The Hindu said they were rescued from four premises, and The Times of India said police searched hostels in Begumpet, Uppal and other areas. The Times of India also reported that police said agents offered ₹30,000 to ₹50,000 for egg donation.

The commission had earlier issued notices to eight ART centres and egg banks over suspected irregularities, The Hindu reported. About 10 days before Wednesday, police sought documents from 14 fertility centres, including consent forms and electronic records of egg donation procedures, to establish how many women were approached, how often they underwent the procedure and whether consent was obtained.
Sharada said the commission would pursue the matter until the investigation is completed.
keyFacts: Commission chairperson Nerella Sharada and member Uzma Shakeer met Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla on November 25.
Police arrested eight people in the case after the racket was busted on October 31.
Sources report 43 or 48 women rescued; PTI and The Hindu say 43.
The commission wants a high-level committee and amendments to the ART Act.
Police sought records from 14 fertility centres; the commission issued notices to eight.
stories.background: Malkajgiri police announced the arrests on October 31, saying women from several states had been recruited and housed in Hyderabad for egg donation procedures at fertility centres. The High Court has denied anticipatory bail to the accused, according to the commission.
stories.whyItMatters: The commission's request seeks wider scrutiny of fertility centres and changes to the ART Act, which would affect how egg donation is regulated and how women recruited for it are protected.

stories.headline: Three workers die inside septic tank at Hyderabad apartment; rights panel seeks report
stories.dek: Police have registered a case against the owner of HR Enviro Protection System, which the FIR says sent the men in without safety equipment or supervision.
stories.summary: Three workers from Srikakulam died after inhaling toxic gas in a septic tank at Dinesh Auric Apartments in Bachupally on November 24. The Telangana Human Rights Commission has sought reports from the state government and the district administration by December 22.
body: Three workers died after inhaling toxic gas while cleaning a septic tank at Dinesh Auric Apartments in Bachupally, Hyderabad, on Tuesday, November 24, according to an FIR registered at Bachupally police station.
The dead are K Shanmukha Rao, also called Suman, 26; Y Pavan, 20; and Suresh Gajiki, 24. All three were natives of Srikakulam district in Andhra Pradesh.

The FIR says Shanmukha Rao and Pavan worked as sewage treatment plant operators for HR Enviro Protection System. South First reported that Suresh had been brought to the apartment after being told the company would give him a job.

The complaint was filed by Suresh's brother-in-law. He said Suresh took him to meet Shanmukha Rao at the apartment at about 10:30 am. Shanmukha Rao was cleaning the tank and lost consciousness while the complainant stood outside watching.
Pavan went in to help and also stopped responding. Suresh entered the tank at about 11.30 am and likewise did not respond. The complainant called out to them, then informed his elder brother.
The News Minute reported that fire department personnel and teams from the Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA) carried out rescue operations, but all three men were dead.

The FIR accuses the company and its owner, identified as Ravi, of sending the men into the tank without adequate safety equipment, protective gear or supporting staff to supervise. It also says two people, identified as Sai and Arif, were at the apartment at the time. The complainant has sought legal action against the company and its owner.

According to The News Minute, a case has been registered against Ravi under Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which covers culpable homicide not amounting to murder. The outlet said the FIR does not cite the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013, which it said does not cover septic tanks.

The Telangana Human Rights Commission (TGHRC), headed by Chairperson Dr Justice Shameem Akther, has taken suo motu cognisance. It has asked the Secretary of the Municipal Administration and Urban Development Department for a report on the circumstances, the safety rules for septic tank and STP sump cleaning, and the responsibility of the apartment management and the contractor.

It has also sought details of inspections, action taken against those responsible, and steps to prevent similar incidents. The Medchal-Malkajgiri District Collector and District Magistrate must report on the circumstances, coordination between departments, and relief or ex-gratia compensation for the families.
Both authorities have been directed to submit their reports by December 22, 2026.
keyFacts: Three workers died in a septic tank at Dinesh Auric Apartments, Bachupally, on November 24.
The dead were aged 26, 20 and 24, all from Srikakulam district.
A case has been registered against HR Enviro owner Ravi under BNS Section 105.
TGHRC has asked for reports from state and district authorities by December 22, 2026.
stories.background: In October 2023, the Supreme Court held that failing to provide minimum protective gear and cleaning devices to workers in hazardous cleaning jobs amounts to forced labour, which the Constitution prohibits, The News Minute reported.
stories.whyItMatters: The commission's questions on safety rules, contractor responsibility and compensation will determine what the state and district authorities must disclose about hazardous cleaning work and the dead men's families.

stories.headline: Telangana to spend ₹203 crore on Khelo India Games from December 11
stories.dek: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy reviewed preparations on Wednesday and told officials the event should leave permanent sports infrastructure behind, with ministers to oversee districts.
stories.summary: Telangana will host the Khelo India Games in Hyderabad from December 11 to 22, with more than 9,000 athletes and officials expected. The state is spending ₹203 crore, and the Centre ₹21 crore.
body: Telangana will host the Khelo India Games from December 11 to 22, with more than 9,000 athletes and officials expected, Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy was told at a review meeting in Hyderabad on Wednesday.

The state government is spending ₹203 crore on the Games, of which ₹120 crore is earmarked for stadium upgrades and sports equipment, according to The Times of India. The Centre is contributing ₹21 crore, a press release said.

Officials told the meeting that works and equipment procurement for the 27 disciplines would be completed by the end of November. Works at 14 stadiums are finished, and the remaining six are due by month-end.

The inaugural ceremony is to be held at LB Stadium on December 11. The Times of India reported that the closing ceremony will be at Gachibowli Stadium on December 22; Siasat, citing the press release, named the GMC Balayogi Stadium as the closing venue.

Reddy directed officials to hold the ceremonies on a grand scale and create a sporting atmosphere across Hyderabad. He told the police and Municipal Administration department to coordinate so that participants and visitors have no cause for complaint.

He also directed the state's vigilance and enforcement wing to monitor stadium works for quality and malpractice, the press release said. The Hindu reported that he warned he would not tolerate lapses in the quality of renovation work.

Ministers will serve as district in-charges. Jupally Krishna Rao has Mahbubnagar, Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy has Warangal, Adluri Lakshman Kumar has Karimnagar and Tummala Nageswara Rao has Khammam. Government adviser P. Sudarshan Reddy will oversee Nizamabad. Sports Minister Vakiti Srihari will coordinate with Ministers D. Sridhar Babu and Ponnam Prabhakar.

The state has held training camps for 1,334 Telangana athletes across 27 disciplines, and sports kits are being given to 861 athletes and coaches, The Times of India reported. Karra Samu, a traditional Telangana martial art, will feature as a demonstration sport.

"The event should not be limited to hosting a national-level sporting competition but should also create permanent sports infrastructure and encourage youngsters to take up sports as a career," Reddy said.
keyFacts: The Games run from December 11 to 22 in Hyderabad, with 27 disciplines.
Telangana is spending ₹203 crore; the Centre is contributing ₹21 crore.
Works at 14 stadiums are complete; six more are due by the end of November.
1,334 Telangana athletes have attended training camps across 27 disciplines.
Karra Samu will be a demonstration sport.
stories.background: Siasat, citing a government press release, said this is the first national event of this scale in Telangana since the National Games of 2002, when about 8,000 sportspersons and officials took part. Reddy invited Prime Minister Narendra Modi to the opening and closing ceremonies on November 15, when he and Union Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya unveiled the logo and mascot of the eighth edition in Delhi.
stories.whyItMatters: The state says the stadium upgrades and equipment will remain after the Games, giving athletes in Telangana permanent facilities rather than temporary arrangements.

stories.headline: Kerala HC disposes of Chennithala's plea after CBI says it found no evidence in Titanium case
stories.dek: Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala did not press his petition once the CBI filed a refer report in the 2006 Travancore Titanium effluent plant case.
stories.summary: The Kerala High Court on Wednesday disposed of Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala's plea in the Travancore Titanium case after the CBI said it found insufficient evidence. Chennithala, who called the case politically motivated, did not press his petition.
body: The Kerala High Court on Wednesday, November 25, disposed of a petition by Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala in the Travancore Titanium corruption case after the CBI told the court it had found insufficient evidence against him.

The agency informed the Single Bench of Justice C. Jayachandran that it had filed a refer report in the case. Chennithala's counsel then told the court that the petition would not be pressed in light of that report, The Hindu reported. Scroll, citing Bar and Bench, said the court accepted the decision.

Scroll reported that the petition was filed in 2014 and challenged the CBI investigation against Chennithala. The Hindu described it as a plea to quash a First Information Report in which he was named an accused. South First reported that the court closed proceedings after accepting the CBI's closure report.

Chennithala welcomed the outcome and alleged that the case was politically motivated, according to South First and Scroll. South First reported that he said he was Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee president when the alleged irregularities took place and had no role in government files or administrative decisions.
Former Chief Minister Oommen Chandy and Indian Union Muslim League leader V.K. Ebrahim Kunju, a former Industries Minister, were also among those named in the case, the reports said.

The case concerns alleged corruption in setting up an effluent treatment plant at the state-owned Travancore Titanium Products Ltd. in Thiruvananthapuram. The project was estimated at ₹256 crore, according to South First and Scroll. South First said the Vigilance Department initially detected alleged irregularities of around ₹66 crore.

The central allegation was that contracts for equipment were awarded to foreign companies in Britain and Finland without inviting a global tender. Investigators also examined claims that payments for the second phase were released before the first phase was complete, South First reported.
The Vigilance Department began a preliminary inquiry in 2006. The High Court directed the CBI to take over the investigation in 2023, The Hindu and Scroll reported.
keyFacts: The Kerala High Court disposed of Chennithala's plea on Wednesday, November 25, 2026.
The CBI filed a refer report citing insufficient evidence.
The effluent treatment plant project was estimated to cost ₹256 crore.
The High Court directed the CBI to take over the probe in 2023.
Oommen Chandy and V.K. Ebrahim Kunju were also named in the case.
stories.background: The case dates to 2006 and concerns an effluent treatment plant at Travancore Titanium Products Ltd. in Thiruvananthapuram. The Vigilance Department began a preliminary investigation that year and sought help from international agencies because foreign companies were involved. South First reported that the probe moved to the CBI after a former employee's 2013 complaint and State government recommendations.
stories.whyItMatters: The CBI's refer report ends the agency's case against Chennithala, who is now Kerala's Home Minister, on the evidence it has gathered.

stories.headline: Kochi's unsafe Chander Kunj Army towers to be imploded by mid-April
stories.dek: Authorities signed a six-month contract with Edifice Engineering on November 21 for the demolition of Towers B and C at Vyttila, 22 months after the High Court's order.
stories.summary: Authorities have signed an agreement with Mumbai-based Edifice Engineering to demolish the two unsafe Chander Kunj Army towers in Kochi by controlled implosion. The blast is expected in early-to-mid April 2027, though no date has been fixed.
body: Authorities signed an agreement on November 21 with Mumbai-based Edifice Engineering to demolish the structurally unsafe Chander Kunj Army Towers B and C at Vyttila in Kochi by controlled implosion, with the blast expected in early-to-mid April 2027.

The agreement was signed by Fort Kochi Revenue Divisional Officer G Sai Krishna, representing the Army Welfare Housing Organisation (AWHO) and the High Court-appointed Executive Committee headed by the Ernakulam District Collector. Shaji Koshy, project manager and authorised signatory, signed for Edifice.

The contractor will bring down the two 26-storey towers at Silver Sand Island, remove the debris and clear the site up to the pile caps. The schedule provides for 24 weeks of core work, plus 15 days each for mobilisation and demobilisation. The implosion is set for Week 16. A company representative, identified as Mehta, said no specific blast date had been decided and that the timeline would begin only after all apartments are handed over and mobilisation is complete.

Owners of the 208 condemned apartments began handing over keys to AWHO a day before the signing, in the presence of revenue officials. Edifice sources told Onmanorama that about 80 per cent of the flats had been handed over. "We are waiting for all the flats to be handed over. Once everyone gives us the flats, we start full-fledged," a senior official said.

The first task is protecting adjoining Tower A, where 56 families still live. Edifice will erect barricades and shift the sewage treatment plant, transformers and other common utilities. Initial salvaging could begin in 15-20 days, the official said.

The net contract value is ₹9,66,40,689 excluding GST, after adjusting an estimated recoverable scrap value of ₹6,25,15,000. Payment is staged: 25 per cent as mobilisation advance against a ₹1-crore performance bank guarantee, 25 per cent two weeks after the implosion, and 50 per cent after debris disposal and site handover.

IIT Madras will assess Tower A's structural safety before and after the demolition. Because the Kochi Metro viaduct lies about 100 feet and 125 feet from Tower C, according to the logistics plan, Edifice must take a commercial general liability policy of at least ₹75 crore within a month. It needs clearances from PESO, KSEB, Kochi Metro Rail Limited, police, fire authorities and local bodies, and must give two weeks' notice of the blast date.

Tower A residents must be given temporary parking of at least 56 spaces. The contractor must also put up 12-foot-high steel barricades, cover Tower A with hessian cloth and install two misting systems to control dust. Engineering plans for the utility work are due by December 21, 2026.
keyFacts: Agreement signed November 21 with Edifice Engineering for demolition of Towers B and C.
Implosion scheduled for Week 16, likely early-to-mid April 2027; no blast date fixed.
Net contract value is ₹9,66,40,689 excluding GST, after ₹6,25,15,000 scrap adjustment.
Contractor must hold liability insurance of at least ₹75 crore.
56 families still live in adjoining Tower A.
stories.background:
AWHO built the complex in 2018. It developed serious structural problems, and 208 families, largely serving and retired Army personnel and their relatives, vacated Towers B and C. On February 3, 2025, the Kerala High Court ordered demolition and reconstruction after expert assessments flagged severe deterioration. The district collector formed an executive committee on February 12, 2025.

Edifice was selected after a tender on June 1, 2026. Rival bidders, including PK Unique Projects, challenged the choice, but the High Court upheld it in September and November 2026.
stories.whyItMatters: The agreement sets the demolition in motion for 208 displaced families, while 56 families in Tower A must keep living beside the site under safety conditions written into the contract.

stories.headline: Five Malayalis among 13 killed in Ras Al Khaimah bus-truck crash
stories.dek: The bus, carrying 41 passengers back from Oman after visa renewal, hit a truck parked at the roadside; 11 of the dead were Indian nationals.
stories.summary: Thirteen people died when a bus returning from Oman hit a parked truck on Al Watan Road in Ras Al Khaimah on Tuesday. Five of the dead were reported to be Malayalis, though only four have been named.
body: Thirteen people, including five Malayalis according to Onmanorama and South First, were killed on Tuesday when a bus from Oman collided with a truck parked on Al Watan Road in Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates.

The bus was carrying 41 passengers back to the UAE after they completed visa renewal procedures, the reports said. The truck had been parked at the roadside because of a mechanical failure. Eleven people died at the scene and two others died in hospital.

Four of the Malayali victims have been named: Hemanth Puthiyakavil, 29, of Mattannur in Kannur; Ashraf, 53, of Attenganam in Kasaragod; Sangeertha Suresh, 26, of Thalassery; and Mohammed Ashiq of Kochi. The fifth has not been identified. South First reported that unconfirmed accounts suggest more Malayalis may be among the dead.

Mathrubhumi English, which counted four Malayalis, gave a different home town for Ashiq. It listed Mohammad Aashiq, 29, as being from Cherpulassery in Palakkad. The outlets also spell the Thalassery woman's name differently.

Eleven of the 13 dead were Indian nationals, authorities confirmed, according to Mathrubhumi English. Other Indian victims named include Vinod Kumar of Andhra Pradesh, Jignesh of Gujarat and Govindaraj of Tamil Nadu. Mathrubhumi also named Raj Kumar and Raman Kumar of Punjab, Rashid Ali of Uttar Pradesh and Mahima Soni of Rajasthan. A Sri Lankan and a Filipino national also died, Onmanorama reported.

South First said Sangeerthana was working in Abu Dhabi and had recently secured a job in Dubai. Her relatives said she was due to join the new workplace on Wednesday. Her brother also works and lives in the UAE.

On the injured, the sources differ. South First reported 14 injured passengers being treated at hospitals in Ras Al Khaimah. Mathrubhumi English reported 26 injured, of whom 12 were discharged after first aid.

The Indian Consulate posted on X that it was "deeply saddened by the tragic road accident in Ras Al Khaimah that claimed the lives of several people, including Indian nationals". It shared a 24-hour toll-free helpline, 800-46342.
Social worker Faisal Purathur said arrangements to bring the bodies home were under way, led by the Ras Al Khaimah Indian Relief Committee.
keyFacts: Thirteen people died in the crash on Al Watan Road, Ras Al Khaimah, on Tuesday.
Eleven of the dead were Indian nationals; a Sri Lankan and a Filipino also died.
The bus carried 41 passengers returning from Oman after visa renewal procedures.
The Indian Consulate helpline is 800-46342, open 24 hours.
stories.background: The bus was returning from Oman, where passengers had gone to complete visa renewal procedures. The truck it hit had been parked at the roadside after a mechanical failure, according to the reports.
stories.whyItMatters: Families in Kerala and other Indian states are awaiting identification and the return of relatives' bodies, with repatriation arrangements now under way.

stories.headline: Supreme Court proposes to set aside Calcutta HC curb on KMC poll notification
stories.dek: The bench suggested sending the delimitation challenge back to a High Court Division Bench for fresh consideration, with the election notification withheld until then. Both sides return on Monday.
stories.summary: The Supreme Court proposed setting aside a Calcutta High Court order that bars notification of Kolkata Municipal Corporation elections until the ward delimitation challenge is decided. Both sides are to return with instructions on Monday.
body: The Supreme Court on Wednesday proposed setting aside a Calcutta High Court order that barred the State Election Commission from notifying Kolkata Municipal Corporation elections until a challenge to ward delimitation is decided.

A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing a petition by the West Bengal government against the High Court's interim order. According to LiveLaw, the bench suggested that the order be set aside and the matter go back to the High Court for fresh consideration by a Division Bench rather than a single judge. Until the issues are considered afresh, the election notification can be withheld, the bench said.

The court observed orally that elections should not be deferred "unreasonably", LiveLaw reported. It noted that the High Court order had not considered all the factual and legal issues the state had raised.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta appeared for West Bengal. Senior advocates Dr A M Singhvi and Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya appeared for the respondents. Both sides will return with instructions on Monday.

The dispute concerns the state's decision to raise the number of KMC wards from 144 to 209. The government passed a law in the Assembly on August 12 and notified the amended Schedule II of the KMC Act on September 11.

Dipu Das, a former councillor, challenged the exercise in the High Court. His counsel argued that the administrator appointed after the elected board ceased to function could not act as the "Corporation" and recommend a reorganisation of wards. He also alleged gerrymandering to give the ruling party an electoral advantage, without regard to geographical contiguity, compactness and administrative convenience.
Advocate General S N Mitra argued that Section 601 of the KMC Act gives the state ample power to alter the Schedules, with or without a recommendation from the Corporation.

A single judge, Justice Hiranmay Bhattacharyya, declined to stay the delimitation on October 29. On November 6, a Division Bench of Justices Sabyasachi Bhattacharyya and Arjun Ray Mukherjee modified that order. It restrained the Election Commission from calling elections on the basis of the amended schedule until the writ petition is disposed of.

The Division Bench held that the petitioner had made out a sufficiently strong prima facie case for interim protection, in order to keep the petition from being rendered infructuous, The Hindu reported.
The Supreme Court will take up the matter again on Monday.
keyFacts: The Supreme Court heard the West Bengal government's appeal on Wednesday; the matter returns on Monday.
KMC wards would rise from 144 to 209 under the delimitation notified on September 11, 2026.
The Calcutta High Court Division Bench restrained the poll notification on November 6.
A single judge had refused to stay the delimitation on October 29.
stories.background: After the BJP came to power in May 2026, the KMC board led by former Mayor Firhad Hakim and its councillors resigned, and the state appointed administrators to run the corporation. The Hindu reported that Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari had on several occasions voiced a preference for Kolkata and Howrah civic polls by the end of November or early December, and that the BJP had begun selecting candidates.
stories.whyItMatters: The timing of Kolkata's civic elections depends on the outcome, as the corporation has been run by an administrator since the elected board resigned.

stories.headline: Savarkar portrait put up at Kolkata Municipal Corporation HQ draws opposition protest
stories.dek: Trinamool and Congress leaders object to the display at the Councillors' Club; BJP MLA Sajal Ghosh says the criticism is aimed at political gain.
stories.summary: A portrait of V D Savarkar has been installed at the Kolkata Municipal Corporation headquarters alongside seven other figures. Trinamool and Congress leaders object, while BJP MLA Sajal Ghosh says the opposition is creating a needless controversy.
body: A portrait of Hindutva ideologue Vinayak Damodar Savarkar has been installed at the Kolkata Municipal Corporation headquarters, drawing objections from the Mamata All India Trinamool Congress and the Congress, according to The Hindu.

The portrait hangs on the second floor of the KMC Councillors' Club, alongside seven other historical figures, including Syama Prasad Mookerjee, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Rana Pratap and Rani Lakshmibai. The space earlier held images of deceased councillors, which have been moved elsewhere.

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari had announced that a portrait of Mookerjee would be installed at several places, including the KMC headquarters. The Bharatiya Janata Party government has begun putting up portraits and statues of Mookerjee and other figures associated with the party's ideology.

Trinamool leader Baishwanar Chatterjee said the KMC already displays portraits of figures linked to the institution, among them Deshbandhu Chittaranjan Das, Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, Dr Bidhan Chandra Roy and Rabindranath Tagore. He questioned why a portrait of Savarkar, who he said has no connection to the civic body, was suddenly being put up.

Congress leader Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury called it an attempt to 'Savarkarise' the state's legacy. "Those celebrating Savarkar cannot be patriots," he said. He also pointed to the renaming of a Kolkata port, previously named after Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, as the Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port.

BJP MLA and former councillor Sajal Ghosh rejected the criticism, calling it "an unfortunate move to reap political benefits by creating unnecessary controversy". He said Savarkar is directly connected to the freedom struggle, "whether you like him or not", and noted the years Savarkar spent in the Andaman Cellular Jail. Mr Ghosh also asked what connection Ho Chi Minh, Karl Marx and Vladimir Lenin, whose portraits were displayed in the past, have with the country.
The West Bengal government dissolved the KMC board on June 8, 2026, and appointed Municipal Commissioner Smita Pandey as administrator. The Trinamool Congress had run the board for 16 years.
The Calcutta High Court has stayed the KMC elections until petitions challenging delimitation are resolved. The state government has approached the Supreme Court against that order.
keyFacts: Savarkar's portrait is on the second floor of the KMC Councillors' Club, with seven other figures.
The KMC board was dissolved on June 8, 2026; Smita Pandey is administrator.
The Calcutta High Court has stayed KMC polls pending delimitation petitions.
The West Bengal government has challenged the stay in the Supreme Court.
stories.background: The BJP came to power in West Bengal in 2026 and dissolved the Trinamool-run Kolkata Municipal Corporation board in June. The government wants civic elections held at the earliest, but the Calcutta High Court has stayed them while delimitation challenges are heard.
stories.whyItMatters: The dispute adds a political argument over public symbols to the contest for control of the Kolkata civic body, whose elections are held up in court.

stories.headline: Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari says Rajbanshi will be added to Eighth Schedule
stories.dek: Adhikari said he raised the demand with the Union home minister and home secretary on November 19, citing a promise in the BJP's Assembly election manifesto.
stories.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said in Cooch Behar on Wednesday that Rajbanshi will be included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution. He said the issue was raised with the Union home minister on November 19.
body: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Wednesday that the Rajbanshi language will be included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, which lists the country's officially recognised languages.

Mr Adhikari spoke to reporters in Cooch Behar district before inaugurating Ras Utsav festivities, the annual celebration of Radha-Krishna. He said the inclusion was a commitment in the BJP's West Bengal Assembly election manifesto, repeated by several senior party leaders before the polls.

"We raised the issue during a meeting with the Union home minister and the home secretary on November 19 that was attended by me and the state's chief secretary," Mr Adhikari said. The reports did not say what response the Centre gave at that meeting.

He said his government was looking after the Rajbanshi community's language, culture, political aspirations and financial security. Cabinet minister Nisith Pramanik, who belongs to the community, greeted him on arrival. Mr Adhikari later joined the festivities locally.

Mr Adhikari said the community was dissatisfied at losing land ownership in the region, and he held the Left Front government responsible. He also said earlier state governments had given the community little representation in the cabinet, and that his government had done more for it since taking office.

"The Rajbanshi community has always stood by us since 2019," he said. In the recently concluded Assembly elections, the BJP won eight of the nine seats in Cooch Behar district, according to The Hindu.
keyFacts: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari spoke in Cooch Behar on Wednesday, November 25, 2026.
He said Rajbanshi will be included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.
He said the issue was raised with the Union home minister and home secretary on November 19.
The BJP won eight of nine Cooch Behar seats in the recent Assembly elections.
stories.background: The Eighth Schedule lists the languages recognised by the Constitution. The Hindu reported that the BJP promised Rajbanshi's inclusion in its 2026 Assembly election manifesto and that senior party leaders repeated the pledge during campaigning.
stories.whyItMatters: Inclusion in the Eighth Schedule would give Rajbanshi formal constitutional recognition, a long-standing demand of the Rajbanshi community in north Bengal.

stories.headline: Bombay HC asks Railways, state to detail steps to ease Thane-Kalyan overcrowding
stories.dek: A bench led by Chief Justice MC Tripathi directed Central Railway, the BMC and the Maharashtra government to file replies on a petition over commuter deaths.
stories.summary: The Bombay High Court on Wednesday asked the Railways and state authorities to set out the infrastructure needed to ease overcrowding on Mumbai's suburban network, especially the Thane-Kalyan stretch. It directed Central Railway, the BMC and the state to file replies.
body: The Bombay High Court on Wednesday directed the Railways and state authorities to spell out the infrastructure measures needed to ease overcrowding on Mumbai's suburban rail network, particularly the Thane-Kalyan stretch.

A bench of Chief Justice MC Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna was hearing a petition by Sarosh Mehta. The petition seeks implementation of recommendations made by a High Court-appointed committee in an earlier case on commuter deaths from falling off overcrowded trains or crossing tracks.

Mehta told the court that nearly 4,000 people die or are injured every year in railway-related accidents across Mumbai and the Mumbai Metropolitan Region. He said overcrowding and safety problems persisted despite earlier court directions.

He cited the committee's recommendations, which included running trains more often, adding coaches, and changing seating layouts in compartments to create more standing space and let commuters near the doors move inside. The court was told that trains built to carry about 1,000 passengers often carry nearly 5,000 at peak hours.

Advocate Jamshed Mistry, appointed amicus curiae to assist the court, said the earlier proceedings had led to the committee and several recommendations. He said the present petition had a limited scope and concerned the Thane-Kalyan belt, which has seen substantial population growth and infrastructure development.

The bench observed that the region had expanded significantly and that a larger commuter population had added to congestion. It noted that projects such as the coastal road and metro lines had improved connectivity in Mumbai, but said corresponding measures were needed to relieve pressure on suburban rail services.
Before going into the merits of the petition, the court said the authorities must consider what additional infrastructure would be needed to ease congestion and allow smoother movement of commuters.

The bench directed Central Railway's General Manager and Divisional Railway Manager, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation and the Maharashtra government to file their replies. It also ordered that the state government be added as a party to the case.
keyFacts: The bench comprised Chief Justice MC Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna.
The petitioner, Sarosh Mehta, said nearly 4,000 people die or are injured yearly in Mumbai and MMR rail accidents.
The court was told trains meant for about 1,000 passengers often carry nearly 5,000 at peak hours.
Central Railway, the BMC and the Maharashtra government must file replies; the state was added as a party.
stories.background: The petition relies on an earlier High Court judgment on deaths of commuters who fell from crowded trains or crossed tracks. That case led to a court-appointed committee, whose recommendations included more frequent trains, extra coaches and modified seating. The present petition is limited to the Thane-Kalyan belt, according to the amicus curiae.
stories.whyItMatters: The replies will show what additional infrastructure the Railways, the BMC and the state say is needed to reduce overcrowding on a network where, the petitioner says, nearly 4,000 people are killed or hurt each year.
