stories.headline: Maharashtra cabinet approves free foodgrains for 42.3 lakh farmers in drought-hit districts
stories.dek: Farmers in 33 districts who are outside existing schemes will get 5 kg of grain a month for three months, as 19 Marathwada dams have dried up.
stories.summary: The Maharashtra cabinet on Wednesday approved free foodgrains for 42.3 lakh farmers in 33 drought-affected districts for three months. Separately, a report cited by Mid-Day said 19 Marathwada dams have run dry and 1,323 tankers are supplying water.
body: The Maharashtra cabinet on Wednesday approved free foodgrains for 42.30 lakh Below Poverty Line farmers in 33 drought-affected districts, for three months, according to a statement issued after its weekly meeting chaired by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis.

Each beneficiary will receive 5 kg a month, made up of 3 kg of rice and 2 kg of wheat. The scheme covers farmers who are not under the direct benefit transfer scheme. The Times of India reported that the relief will be reviewed after three months.

The newspaper said 5.8 crore people covered by the Food Security Act already get free foodgrains, and 21.6 lakh farmers in 14 suicide-affected districts receive Rs 170 a month. The new benefit goes to those who receive neither.

Mid-Day, citing the state government's latest compilation, reported that 19 dams in Marathwada have completely run dry. It said 1,323 water tankers are supplying water to 1,102 villages and 3,801 hamlets across 11 districts, and that tanker demand has reportedly doubled over the past month.

The cabinet sub-committee on drought, led by Revenue Minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule, has also taken decisions. It has made it mandatory to build embankments connected to every new bridge on rivers and streams under agencies including the Public Works Department, MSRDC, MMRDA, CIDCO, Naina and the Mukhyamantri Gram Sadak Yojana. Bawankule said the aim is to raise storage capacity by blocking at least one metre of water under each bridge.

The sub-committee also permitted fodder camps wherever necessary and extended to June 30 a scheme under which silt from gram panchayat and zilla parishad water bodies is given free to farmers. It decided on a final grant of Rs 5,000, plus NDRF/SDRF assistance, for forest-land holders and farmers without land records who actually cultivate land.

A proposal has been sent to raise wages under the rural employment guarantee scheme in the state from Rs 317 to Rs 375 to prevent labour migration. The cabinet also sanctioned ₹5,548 crore for the Narmada-Tapi River-linking Project in Nandurbar district. An MoU on supplying silt for highway construction is to be signed in the winter session of the state assembly.

1,323 tankers supply 1,102 villages and 3,801 hamlets across 11 districts.
The cabinet sanctioned ₹5,548 crore for the Narmada-Tapi River-linking Project in Nandurbar.

stories.headline: BMC proposes handing two more reserved Bandra plots to slum project developer
stories.dek: Congress corporator Karen D'Mello has asked Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis to stop the plan, while a ward official says the developer would only maintain the land.
stories.summary: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation has proposed handing two plots reserved for public amenities at Bandra Reclamation to a private developer for 15 years. A Congress corporator and residents object; a ward official says the developer would only maintain the land.
body: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has proposed handing two plots reserved for public amenities at Bandra Reclamation to a private developer for 15 years, drawing objections from a local corporator and residents, Hindustan Times reported.

The plots are a recreation ground of about 3,300 square metres and a health dispensary plot, with an adjoining road, of about 4,300 square metres. Both are next to a slum rehabilitation project. They are meant to go to the developer executing that project for plantation, beautification and maintenance.
The land was handed to the BMC by the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) and is reserved for public amenities under the Development Plan 2034.

Karen D'Mello, the Congress corporator for the area, wrote to Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on November 12. She questioned why the plots should be handed over when the BMC has the resources to develop and maintain a garden itself. She also said she feared they could eventually come under private development.

D'Mello also raised concerns over reports of a proposed mini golf course and other sporting facilities on the plots. She asked the BMC to withdraw the proposal and develop both plots itself. "A recreation ground plot should remain accessible for recreation and the health dispensary land should be developed for public healthcare rather than placed under a private entity's control," she said in the letter.

A senior official from the H-West ward said the proposal followed applicable rules and regulations. "It is not as if we are giving the plots to the developer. Instead, they will merely take care of the upkeep and beautification of the plots," the official said.

Asif Zakaria, a former Bandra corporator, said the plan goes against the BJP-led civic administration's decision to discontinue the caretaker policy. "We have seen umpteen open spaces being usurped by private entities under the guise of caretaker arrangements," he said. He added that a golf course, if built, would be of no use to local residents.
Furkan Shaikh, a Bandra resident, said: "Public land must remain public, in ownership, access and spirit."

HT reported on June 3 that 394 recreation ground plots across Mumbai are maintained by contractors rather than the BMC. It also reported that many such plots have not been formally handed over by developers, who often merge them into their private plots.
keyFacts: The BMC proposes handing two Bandra Reclamation plots to a developer for 15 years.
The recreation ground is about 3,300 sq m; the dispensary plot and road about 4,300 sq m.
Karen D'Mello wrote to Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on November 12.
An H-West ward official said the developer would only maintain and beautify the plots.
stories.background: The proposal follows the Bombay High Court's stay on the BMC's bid to convert the Neville D'Souza Football Ground in Bandra West into an exhibition and convention centre.
stories.whyItMatters: Residents of Bandra would be affected if land reserved for a recreation ground and a health dispensary comes under a private developer's care for 15 years.
